DNA flow cytometry is not a useful prognostic tool for patients with solid tumors, but that it may be useful for the characterization of tumor cell populations and the classification of cancer types.
ploidy and cell cycle parameters are important prognostic factors, but only in combination with histopathologic diagnosis.
the DNA content and cytokinetic information obtained by flow cytometry is an independent prognostic indicator in patients with cancer.

ploidy, but not G1/100, is a prognostic factor in cancer.
ploidy and proliferating activity are important factors in determining the clinical behavior of solid tumors.

The main takeaway from our work is that
DNA ploidy and cytokinesis are powerful predictors of survival in patients with solid tumors.
ploidy and cell cycle parameters are not independent prognostic factors.
